slides.title: Classmethods vs Staticmethods Overview
slides.prompt: Classmethods receive the class itself ('cls') as their first argument and can access class state. Staticmethods receive no implicit first argument and behave like regular plain functions scoped within the class namespace.

slides.title: Use Case for Classmethods
slides.prompt: What is a primary software design use case for applying the @classmethod decorator in Python?
options: Creating alternative constructors (factory methods) that parse different data formats to instantiate objects
Preventing child classes from overriding base class methods
Converting dynamic attributes into constant values at runtime
Enforcing type checking on method arguments
slides.correctAnswer: Creating alternative constructors (factory methods) that parse different data formats to instantiate objects

slides.title: Accessing Class Variables
slides.prompt: Fill in the parameter name used inside a classmethod to modify a class variable.

slides.title: Difference Between Instance, Class, and Static Methods
slides.prompt: Which statement correctly distinguishes staticmethods from instance methods and classmethods?
options: Staticmethods do not automatically receive an implicit first argument ('self' or 'cls')
Staticmethods cannot be called directly from class names
Staticmethods can modify private instance attributes directly
Staticmethods must return an instance of the class
slides.correctAnswer: Staticmethods do not automatically receive an implicit first argument ('self' or 'cls')
